newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine grain/oils forecast revised up.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine grain/oils forecast revised up.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINIAN GRAIN AND SUNSEED CROP FORECAST REVISED UPWARDS

KIEV, July 10 - As a result of favourable weather conditions in late May and June, we have revised upward our forecast for Ukraine's total grain output to 37-39 million tonnes from 31.0-33.0 million tonnes (Table 1).
As of June 25, 56 percent of winter wheat and winter rye plantings were rated good, 39 percent satisfactory, while poor plantings accounted for only five percent of sowings.
Most corn (maize) and sunflower plantings are also rated good or satisfactory.
Harvesting has started in the southern regions of Crimea, Dnepropetrovsk, Nikolaev and Kherson.

By June 30, about 65,000 hectares of cereals and pulses, mainly spring barley and peas, had been harvested. Per hectare yields are so far 2.59 tonnes, about the same as in 1995 and 60 percent above last year's figure.
